subject: Ops & Performance qualification: streaming targets, concurrency and cost tradeoffs (OptiRetail)
messages:
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Jensen <sarah.jensen@optiretail.com>, Tim Bass <tim.bass@optiretail.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-09-30T15:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Ops discovery - performance targets

Hi Sarah / Tim — thanks for the call earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our side so we can qualify and scope a canary: 

Summary of targets you mentioned
- Latency: p95 generation latency <= 250 ms for interactive flows (typical prompt <= 128 tokens).
- Streaming: clients expect first partial tokens within ~120 ms and steady token streaming thereafter for long responses (up to ~1.5k tokens).
- Throughput & concurrency: peak concurrent requests ~300 RPS (spikey Black Friday-like events), expected sustained 60–80 RPS; estimated concurrent user sessions ~600–800.
- Cost sensitivity: prefer cost-efficient defaults; open to trading slightly higher latency for meaningful cost reduction.

Preliminary cost/perf levers to consider (we'll validate in qualification):
- Continuous batching with a short batching window (10–20ms) for heavy traffic paths.
- Prefix/KV caching for product metadata prompts (saves repeated encoder work across similar prefixes).
- Two-model strategy: smaller low-latency model for interactive browse/search; larger/vetted model variant for long-form/fallback.
- Quantization profiles: q4_0 or q5_0 for non-streaming/rerank jobs; careful verification for streaming correctness.

Requested deliverables from OptiRetail to finalize a canary plan:
1) Representative sample payloads (short/long prompt distributions)
2) Expected QPS schedule for a typical peak day vs flash sales
3) Any hard SLOs for 99th/99.9th percentile (we only discussed p95)

I attached an Ops SLO matrix template and a sample payload schema — please drop your samples and we'll run a sizing exercise. Next internal step: Laura and Dev will propose a concrete canary config (models, batching window, cache strategy) once we have samples.

Thanks,
Dylan Brooks
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
D: +1 415-555-0123

Thanks Dylan — appreciated. Quick clarifications and we've attached a small set of sample payloads (short/med/long) to the shared drive link. Notes: 
- Typical short prompt: 25–60 tokens (product title + 1–2 lines context)
- Median prompt length for recommendations flow: ~140 tokens
- Long prompts (cart summarization + user history): 600–1200 tokens
- We must preserve streaming for the recommendations UI (progressive card population); first token within ~150ms is acceptable if overall p95 stays under 300ms.
- Peak we described is closer to 350 RPS for small regions during promotions; global peak could see ~700 RPS across regions.

We uploaded the sample_payloads.json to the link you referenced. Please advise what metadata you need with each payload (session id, user type, product ids). We can make a test account for your canary.

— Sarah Jensen
Head of Engineering, OptiRetail

From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-02T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Ops sizing thoughts for OptiRetail (internal)

Adding technical context for the tradeoffs we discussed on the call: 
- Continuous batching: gives 1.6–2.2x token throughput uplift on our fleet for steady high-load routes. Downside: slightly increases median latency for singletons when batching window is >20ms. Strategy: hybrid policy — keep window at 10–15ms for interactive routes, allow 25–30ms for background/rerank paths.
- KV/prefix caching: will be high ROI for product-title-driven prompts. If OptiRetail provides product-id keyed prefixes we can cache encoder side and avoid repeated prefix recomputation. Expect ~25–40% token-cost reduction for those flows.
- Quantization: q4_0 gives ~1.8x inference throughput for decoder steps with modest perf delta on quality for classification/short generation. For streaming we need to validate generation stability; propose trial on small subset.
- Model variants: propose two rollout candidates:
  • rw-small-v2 (optimized for low-latency, smaller context) as primary for recommendations UI
  • rw-large-q4 (quantized) as fallback for long-form/cart summarization to save cost
- Canary config idea: 72-hour canary with mixed traffic (60% small model, 40% large-q4) and controlled ramp to 50 RPS initial, then step up. Collect p50/p95/p99, token-cost, and tail-samples for quality regression checks.

I've generated a rough cost estimate and attached redwood-cost-estimate.pdf. Laura — can you convert these rough numbers into a per-hour canary budget for the proposal?

— Dev
Senior Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
attachments: redwood-cost-estimate.pdf (pdf)

Sarah / Tim — thanks for the quick turn. Consolidating actions and owners so we can get the canary scheduled: 
1) OptiRetail: drop full sample payload set to the shared drive + tag payloads with session_id, user_type, and product_id (owner: Sarah) — target: 2026-10-05
2) Redwood (Dev/Laura): finalize canary config (batch window, caching keys, model routing), produce step-up schedule and per-hour budget — target: 2026-10-06
3) Security & Access: set up test service account and API key with limited quota for canary (owner: Marissa) — target: 2026-10-04
4) Contract/Procurement: Sales to confirm billing cadence and DocuSign initial canary MSA (owner: Dylan) — I'll post the HS record and DocuSign link once ready.

Also: we'll run two micro-experiments before the canary — (A) confirm streaming fidelity on q4 quantized variant (small sample set), (B) measure cache hit-rate lift with product-id prefixes. Those inform the final cost estimate.

I'll create a brief runbook and share a Slack channel for day-of run. Proposed canary week: 2026-10-12 (flexible).

Dylan
